name: Linux and OS
description: Namespaces, cgroups, seccomp, file systems and the process model. The foundation of every isolation technology and sandbox.
practice: Build a minimal container by hand with unshare and cgroups, limiting CPU, memory and network.

name: Distributed Systems
description: Long-running tasks, state recovery and scheduling are all distributed systems problems at heart.
concepts: Idempotency and the limits of exactly-once
practice: Revisit the Raft lab from MIT 6.5840, focusing on how idempotency and retries are designed.

name: LLM Fundamentals
description: Building an agent platform means understanding the input and output constraints of the model.
practice: Without a framework, call the API directly and implement one multi-turn tool-use exchange.

name: Agent Loop
description: The loop of model, tools and observations: the minimal core of every agent.
concepts: Returning tool errors to the model
practice: Implement a complete agent loop with approval and interruption in under 200 lines.

name: Isolation Technologies
description: Security and performance trade-offs between containers, gVisor, Firecracker and Kata.
practice: On one machine, compare the startup latency and syscall overhead of the three runtimes.

name: Code Execution Sandbox
description: The environment where agents write and run code, and the core product of agent infrastructure.
practice: Build a code execution service with an API on top of Firecracker or gVisor.

name: Relational Databases and SQL
description: Transactions, indexes and query optimization: the state foundation of most backend services.
practice: Design indexes for a table with tens of millions of rows and compare query plans and latency before and after.

name: Caching
description: Trade memory for latency and throughput while handling consistency and invalidation.
practice: Add a Redis cache to a read-heavy endpoint and load-test its hit rate and P99.
